SafeSphere is a privacy-focused women\'s safety platform being built in phases as a final-year project.
This build has real accounts, a Safety Circle, a manual SOS session and Safe Walk with check-ins. During SOS or a Safe Walk, your location can be saved to your own records. Your Safety Circle is texted from your phone only if you switch on automatic SMS. During an active SOS you can record audio, photos or video as evidence: only when you tap, always with a visible notification, encrypted on your phone at once and uploaded to your private Evidence Vault. SafeSphere never contacts emergency services and never records in the background on its own.
Suggested recovery passphrases use the EFF Large Wordlist by the Electronic Frontier Foundation (CC BY 3.0). Passphrases are checked against the 10k-most-common password list from the SecLists project (MIT licence).
These terms are a placeholder for the Phase 1 prototype. Final terms of use will be written and reviewed before SafeSphere is released to the public.

This is a placeholder for the current prototype, not a final policy.
In this build SafeSphere sends your name, email and password to the SafeSphere server to create and check your account. The server stores your name and email, and only a one-way hash of your password. This device stores your name, email and a sign-in token so you stay signed in.
Location: only while an emergency is active, and only if you allow it, your phone\'s location (with its accuracy and the battery level) is saved to your own emergency record on the SafeSphere server. Only you can see the saved points; the only place your location goes beyond that is a map link in the Safety Circle SMS, and only if you switch on automatic SMS or send it yourself (see below). Points that are waiting to be uploaded are kept in memory, not stored on the phone. Location points are deleted together with the emergency record and your account.
Safe Walk: the server stores the walk (optional destination text you type, check-in times, missed check-ins) and only the LATEST location of your phone during the walk, which replaces the previous one. No route or track is kept. Nobody is contacted unless you switch on automatic SMS (see below).
Stop and route checks (if switched on): the destination text you type is looked up with your phone\'s map service (Google on most phones) and its coordinates are stored with the walk. Your phone compares its position with the direct route in memory only; no movement history is stored on the phone or the server. When a walk ends normally, its destination coordinates and last location are deleted from the server; if it ended in an emergency they are kept with that walk.
Safety Circle SMS (only if you switch on automatic SMS, or when you tap Text yourself): your phone sends an SMS to your enabled contacts with your name, the time, what happened and a map link to your last location. To work without internet, your enabled contacts\' names and numbers are kept on this phone (deleted when you log out). The server records only that a message was sent, to which contact and its status; never the number or the text. Tapping Call 112 opens your phone\'s dialer; SafeSphere records that it was opened, not whether you called.
Evidence Vault (only during an active SOS, only when you tap): audio from your microphone, or a photo or video taken with your phone\'s own camera app. Each item is encrypted on this phone right away with its own key, which is protected by your phone\'s secure hardware; the unencrypted file is deleted. The SafeSphere server receives only the encrypted file, its size, two fingerprints (SHA-256), the capture times and a chain-of-custody log; it cannot open the evidence. If the server offers a vault recovery key, a copy of each item\'s key is sealed for it, so the evidence can still be recovered if your phone is lost; that recovery key is kept offline by the SafeSphere operator, not on the server. If you set up a recovery passphrase, the server also stores a copy of each item\'s key locked with a key that only your passphrase opens; the passphrase itself never leaves your phone, so SafeSphere cannot read it or reset it (someone holding the server\'s data could try to guess a weak passphrase, which is why short or common ones are refused). The server records when that locked copy was last fetched. No location, file name or device details are sent with evidence. You can delete evidence everywhere with your password once the emergency has ended. The camera app you use may keep its own copy; check its settings. SafeSphere does not read your phone\'s contacts or your messages.
A complete privacy policy will be published before any feature that handles more personal data is released.
